title: Cliffside Retail — Quick outreach angles and objection scripts
content:
Purpose: quick personal scratchpad for cold outreach + pilot framing for Cliffside Retail (mid-sized omnichannel retailer). Keep it informal — raw thoughts, call openers, objections, quick research bullets.

Context notes (raw):
- Cliffside Retail: ~180 stores, regional (Pacific NW), omni ecomm + brick. Known for fast returns, loyalty program. Tech org moderate maturity — uses Shopify Plus + custom OMS, in-house data team of ~8. Heard rumor they run on AWS with restricted third-party integrations for PII.
- Why we care: use-case fits for in-store assistant (POS agent), returns automation + customer service triage, product search reranking to boost AOV. Could be Dedicated or Private depending on PII concerns.
- Key contacts to find: Head of Digital (likely Kate Morales), Director of Customer Support (Samir Patel), Head of Store Ops (Toni Nguyen), Security contact (infosec manager).

Quick business hooks (one-liners to test):
- "Cut chat & phone answer time in half for returns and basic tracking questions — without hiring more agents."
- "Improve product search relevance on mobile by surfacing complementary items at checkout"
- "Pilot a store associate assistant that surfaces quick SKU info, stock levels, and approved return policies — latency-sensitive, needs private network option."

Outbound sequence (sketch):
- Email 1 (cold) subject: Quick idea to shave minutes off store returns
  Body bullets: 1) short problem statement 2) one potential metric (reduce avg handle time by 40%) 3) suggest 15-min pilot call to validate top 3 use-cases
- Email 2 (follow-up 4 days) — add short customer example + ask for intro to Samir/Toni
- LinkedIn: short note to Head of Digital referencing a 2-slide pilot one-pager
- Call script opener: "Hi [Name], saw you scale returns last Q — curious if a lightweight pilot that routes 60% of basic queries away from CS is interesting?"

Pilot framing (6-week lightweight):
- Goals: reduce returns handling time, measure deflection of basic CS questions, measure search CTR uplift on targeted SKUs
- Success metric: 25% reduction in returns handling time OR 10% lift in add-to-cart for recommended complements
- Scope: 5 stores + website checkout search, connect to read-only inventory API, no PII stored, use Dedicated/Private for guaranteed latency if requested
- Deliverables: integration plan, evaluation dashboard (latency/cost/accuracy), playbook for handoff to SRE/product

Technical concerns to surface proactively:
- Data privacy: Clarify we can run inference in their VPC/private deployment and integrate with KMS/HSM for keys
- Latency: on-prem or dedicated pool for sub-200ms store assistant flows
- Integration effort: need read-only SKU & inventory endpoint, sample of their chat transcripts (redacted) for prompt tuning
- Cost: present cost per session and per-month forecast for pilot vs FTE savings

Objection handling roughs:
- "We can't send customer data offsite": "Totally get it — we can run the pilot in your VPC or on-prem package, and we support KMS integration and audit logs. For an initial run we only need redacted transcripts or synthetic data to validate routing logic."
- "LLM hallucinations / product accuracy concerns": "Pilot scope includes validation layer for SKU responses — we keep answer generation constrained to inventory-backed facts and fall back to a verified KB. Also we'll provide confidence thresholds and QA sample review streams."
- "We don't have the engineering bandwidth": "We can scope a read-only webhook + lightweight mapping layer — typical pilot is ~2 engineer-weeks from customer's side (one backend + one PM). We also offer professional services to own integration for an extra fee."
- "Cost concerns (per-token pricing)": "For latency-sensitive flows we recommend Dedicated pools with batching/caching to reduce per-token cost; pilot terms include usage credit and a capped spend estimate tied to pilot goals."

Example quick pitch lines for voicemails / intros:
- "Quick note — we help retailers like you reduce returns handling time with an in-store assistant that integrates to inventory in under 6 weeks. Can I grab 15 minutes next week?"
- "We ran a small pilot with a regional brand — they saw 18% CS deflection in month one. I think Cliffside could get similar results for returns flows."

Research snippets (to verify before outreach):
- Verify platform: Shopify Plus + custom OMS? check job postings for "Platform Engineer - Cliffside" and LinkedIn tech stack
- Quarterly results / press: look for store openings, any mention of seasonal return surges
- Competitor behavior: any public case studies from companies in region using AI chat/assistants at POS

Questions for Diego / Priya to fill in:
- Priya: can you surface any redacted chat transcript samples we can use to show routing example in outreach?
- Diego: draft a 2-slide pilot one-pager and a short cost estimate for 5-store pilot (include dedicated pool option)

Next steps (personal):
- Pull LinkedIn names for Kate Morales, Samir Patel, Toni Nguyen (today)
- Quick scrape of career page & tech stack (tomorrow morning)
- Draft email 1 & pilot one-pager (by EOD)
- If we don't hear back in a week, try intro via partner channel (payment processor?)

Loose notes / mental checklist:
- Keep outreach short, metric-oriented, avoid heavy product jargon in first touch
- Attach one-pager that highlights security (VPC, KMS), latency (dedicated), success metric
- Prep a short demo script: simple conversation where store associate asks "is this returnable?" and system responds citing policy + SKU availability.

Random sideways ideas (brainstorm):
- Offer to run a 'black-box' A/B ranking test for checkout recommendations for 2 weeks to show immediate ROI without backend integration (client provides CSV of impressions/clicks).
- Position Redwood Optimize as a cost-savings audit post-pilot to lock-in committed capacity for Dedicated pools.

Tagline for messaging experiments: "Fewer returns, faster answers — pilot in 6 weeks."

—— END SCRATCHPAD —
Notes: keep iterations here; will convert to a tidy one-pager once contacts confirmed.
